claims.text: The JavaScript SDK is installed from @dashevo/evo-sdk; this course pins version 4.1.1.
EvoSDK.testnetTrusted() creates a client configured for testnet, and await sdk.connect() establishes its connection.
sdk.system.status() returns a StatusResponse whose JSON form includes network.chainId and chain.latestBlockHeight.
Connecting and reading system status needs no identity, wallet, mnemonic, or funded balance.

examples.purpose: Install Evo SDK 4.1.1, connect a trusted testnet client, read system status, and print the responding chain ID and current Platform height.
examples.verification: fixture API-shape assertions and a manually observed read-only testnet run on 2026-09-10

priorKnowledge: content/academy/why-build-on-dash.mdx — the learner has chosen which ticket-marketplace state belongs on Platform
content/academy/what-is-dash-platform.mdx — the learner recognizes Platform and DAPI but has not used the SDK
teachingPlan.centralQuestion: What is the smallest program that proves a local Node project can talk to Dash Platform testnet?
teachingPlan.likelyMistake: Treating successful SDK construction as proof that a live DAPI request worked, or adding wallet secrets to a read-only setup.
teachingPlan.workedExample: The developer connects the ticket-marketplace project to testnet and prints the live chain ID and Platform block height.
reasoningChain: The marketplace architecture needs a working connection before it can create anything.
A pinned SDK installation makes the following code reproducible.
Constructing and connecting a client opens the path to testnet, but a status request proves data came back.
The returned chain ID distinguishes testnet, and the changing height shows live state rather than copied output.
Because the operation only reads public status, wallet setup and funding can wait for later lessons.

coverageMap.explanation: Start a Node project explains the exact 4.1.1 install and why it is pinned.

assessment: fixture asserts the pinned install command and imports the installed package

coverageMap.explanation: Make one live read explains testnetTrusted() and connect() without endpoint-selection internals.
coverageMap.demonstration: connect.mjs constructs the testnet client and awaits sdk.connect().
assessment: fixture constructs the same client and checks the connect API exists
learner confirms the returned chain ID identifies testnet

coverageMap.explanation: Make one live read distinguishes opening a connection from receiving a decoded status response.
coverageMap.demonstration: connect.mjs awaits sdk.system.status() and prints network.chainId plus chain.latestBlockHeight.
assessment: fixture checks every status-read API and output accessor
learner runs the script and sees both live values

readerReview.reasoningChain: A project that has only an architecture needs a reproducible SDK installation, then a configured testnet client, then a request whose returned values prove the connection did useful work. Since status is public and read-only, secrets and funding don't belong yet.
readerReview.transferQuestion: A script constructs an EvoSDK testnet client but never sends a request. Has the developer proved DAPI is reachable?
readerReview.answer: No. The script must await a live method such as sdk.system.status() and receive its decoded response.
